facts.statement: Fossils of Iharkutosuchus were found in the Santonian-aged Csehbánya Formation in the Bakony Mountains of western Hungary.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in the Santonian-aged (Late Cretaceous) Csehbánya Formation in the Bakony Mountains of western Hungary.

facts.statement: Iharkutosuchus had a low skull and a short snout.
facts.quote: Its skull was low, and the snout was short.

facts.statement: Iharkutosuchus is unusual for having heterodont teeth, with some being complex and multicusped like mammal teeth.
facts.quote: Iharkutosuchus is unusual in its heterodonty: some of its teeth were complex and multicusped, like mammal teeth.

facts.statement: The genus Iharkutosuchus was described in 2007 by Attila Ősi and colleagues.
facts.quote: The genus was described in 2007 by Attila Ősi and colleagues.

facts.statement: The name Iharkutosuchus means "Iharkút crocodile" and refers to the site where it was found.
facts.quote: Iharkutosuchus (nombre que significa "cocodrilo de Iharkút", por el sitio en que fue hallado) es un género extinto de crocodiliforme eusuquio basal.

facts.statement: The type species, I. makadii, was named in honor of László Makádi.
facts.quote: La especie tipo es I. makadii, nombrada en honor de László Makádi.

facts.statement: Iharkutosuchus lived during the Santonian age, between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Research in 2026 reported Hunter-Schreger band-like patterns and wavy enamel in Iharkutosuchus teeth, which are interpreted as adaptations for a herbivorous diet and high-efficiency chewing.
facts.quote: Prondvai et al. (2026) report evidence of Hunter-Schreger band-like patterns in the tooth enamel of Iharkutosuchus (interpreted as differing in structural origin from Hunter-Schreger bands of mammals), as well as evidence of wavy enamel in the studied crocodyliform (a feature also known in ornithopod dinosaurs), interpreted as likely adaptations to a herbivorous diet and high-efficiency chewing.

rejected.quote: Iharkutosuchus is an extinct genus of basal eusuchian crocodyliform.
